metadata.title: Evaluation and Management of Kidney Dysfunction in Advanced Heart Failure: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
top_takeaways: Kidney dysfunction in advanced heart failure involves complex hemodynamic and neurohormonal derangements that may recover or stabilize with optimal decongestion and guideline-directed medical therapy.

Quantifying underlying irreversible intrinsic kidney disease versus reversible functional impairment is essential when evaluating candidates for advanced surgical therapies, such as durable LVAD or heart transplantation.
Integrated palliative care and tailored shared decision-making processes are critical components of care for patients with co-existing advanced heart failure and advanced kidney disease.

recommendations.statement: Optimization of volume status and implementation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) are recommended in patients with advanced heart failure to stabilize kidney function and reverse hemodynamic or neurohormonal renal derangements.

recommendations.target_population: Patients with advanced heart failure and secondary kidney dysfunction
